items.headline: S&P 500 sinks 1.2% in worst day in a month
items.detail: The S&P 500 fell 90.66 points (-1.2%) to 7,408.30; the Dow lost 506.93 points (-1.0%) to 51,711.65 and the Nasdaq slid 2.2% to 25,137.69.
items.why: A megacap-tech earnings slump collided with crude oil spiking past $102/bbl on escalating Middle East conflict, reigniting inflation and AI-spending fears.

items.headline: Alphabet and Tesla lead a megacap rout
items.detail: Alphabet dropped about 7% and Tesla fell roughly 14-15% after their earnings reports, dragging the Nasdaq down more than 2%.
items.why: Both reports intensified worries that heavy AI capital spending is outrunning near-term profit, triggering the worst megacap selloff in weeks.

items.headline: Oil surge past $102 is the macro swing factor
items.detail: US crude climbed above $102/bbl (up ~31% since July 2), lifting Treasury yields and pressuring rate-sensitive equities.
items.why: Escalation in the Iran/Middle East conflict is squeezing supply and reviving inflation expectations, which weighs on stock valuations.

items.headline: Nifty extends losing streak to five sessions
items.detail: The Nifty 50 slid below 23,650 and the Sensex fell 331.62 points (-0.43%) to 76,059.77, though both recovered off morning lows.
items.why: Elevated crude, geopolitical tension and persistent foreign selling kept sentiment cautious despite an intraday bounce.

items.headline: Auto, energy and metals drag; IT outperforms
items.detail: Auto, energy and metal stocks led the decline while IT names outperformed and Bank Nifty ended marginally higher.
items.why: Higher oil raises input-cost and margin fears for autos and energy-heavy sectors, while defensive/export-linked IT drew relative buying.

items.headline: Crude near $100 and FPI selling pressure the rupee
items.detail: Brent briefly crossed $100/bbl and foreign portfolio investors kept offloading in the cash segment; the Nifty lost 2.33% and Sensex 2.70% on the week.
items.why: A higher oil bill widens India's trade deficit and pressures the rupee, feeding FPI outflows and inflation worries.

items.headline: Record DII buying is cushioning the fall
items.detail: Strong domestic institutional buying — with DII ownership at an all-time high near 20.9% — has limited the downside during heavy foreign selling.

items.headline: Bitcoin slides to ~$65K as risk-off deepens
items.detail: BTC traded around $64,962, down ~1.4% on the day; total crypto market cap fell ~1.3% to about $2.3 trillion and Fear & Greed dropped to 28.
items.why: The same oil-driven, higher-yield risk-off wave hitting equities spilled into crypto as inflation concerns returned.

items.headline: Cooling ETF inflows sap institutional bid
items.detail: US spot Bitcoin ETF net inflows fell from $203.14M on July 21 to just $68.99M on July 22, a 66% drop, despite a seven-day inflow streak.
items.why: Institutional buyers eased off as macro risk rose, removing a key pillar that had been supporting prices.

items.headline: Regulatory hopes fade as Clarity Act odds fall
items.detail: Bitcoin weakened further as confidence dimmed that legislators would advance the Clarity Act in August.
items.why: A narrowing legislative window revived regulatory uncertainty, adding a crypto-specific drag on top of the macro selloff.

items.headline: Solana holds flat; BSOL ETF keeps drawing inflows
items.detail: SOL held near $77.65 (roughly flat on the day, +1% on the week) as Bitwise's Solana ETF (BSOL) added $2.64M, lifting cumulative inflows to about $1.14 billion.
items.why: Steady ETF demand for SOL offset the broader risk-off drag, leaving it more resilient than BTC and ETH.

crossCuttingTheme: Crude oil spiking above $100/bbl on escalating Middle East conflict is the shared driver: it lifts Treasury yields and inflation expectations, fueling a simultaneous risk-off move that hit US equities, dragged the Nifty via a weaker rupee and FPI outflows, and pulled crypto lower as ETF demand cooled.
